MXML Actions

MXML actions allow a callback to show, hide, focus or update elements without writing a separate method for each operation. Actions are validated during compilation and run in the order they are declared.

Example Usage

Understanding the Code

  • OnPressed: Calls App.Save first.
  • Set: Changes the Result text to Saved.
  • Show: Makes Result visible without moving focus.

If the bound callback throws, later actions are not run. Repeated actions are allowed and keep their declaration order. Targets can be declared later in the file.

Available Actions

  • Show: Takes Target and an optional Focus value, which defaults to true.
  • Hide: Takes Target.
  • Toggle: Takes Target and an optional Focus value, which defaults to false.
  • Focus: Takes Target.
  • Set: Takes Target, Property and Value. The property and conversion are checked during compilation.
  • Invoke: Takes Path, pointing to a public parameterless backend method.

An Actions wrapper can be used to group actions. Blocks require a void-returning callback or event. Targets use the current page scope, with paths such as Settings/Name for named child pages. Actions from a replaced document will not operate on its detached or disposed targets.

MXMLFlags

For short sequences, MXMLFlags provides a compact version of the same actions:

Place this property element inside a Button, with Result, Editor, Help and Name declared in its page. Commas or semicolons separate the flags. Show and Toggle accept an optional :true/:false or second comma argument.

Flags append after an existing callback rather than replacing it. Unknown flags, empty arguments and invalid boolean values are compilation errors.

Notes

Declare UI elements normally, then use Show or Hide to change them. UI declarations cannot be embedded inside a callback. To create a modal popup, call ConsoleWindowManager.ShowPopup from a backend method.
